# Domain Rules

<!-- Generated by /ai-context. Manual edits are overwritten on re-run. -->

## AS IS — Current state

### Overview

- A tracking session's lifecycle: `ACTIVE` → `FINISHED`, gated by permission checks and a
  closed set of valid sampling intervals (`domain/session/SessionControllerImpl.kt`).
- Stop-vs-moving time classification over a raw point stream, with inclusive/exclusive
  boundary semantics (`domain/stats/SegmentClassifier.kt`).
- Pure stats derivation (distance, speed, elapsed time) recomputed on demand, never stored
  per point (`domain/stats/StatsEngine.kt`).
- Export file generation restricted to finished sessions, in two fixed formats (`domain/export/`).
- Best-effort, at-most-once reverse geocoding of a session's starting point (`domain/geocoding/`).
- User-configurable settings with typed defaults, reactively observed by every screen
  (`data/settings/SettingsRepository.kt`).

### Sampling interval — closed enum, not runtime validation

- `SamplingInterval` (`domain/model/SamplingInterval.kt`) has exactly 10 members: 1, 3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45, 60, 120, 180 seconds.
- There is no `fromSeconds(Int)` factory — an invalid value is unrepresentable by the type system, not rejected at runtime.
- `SessionControllerImpl.startSession` still calls `isAllowedIntervalSeconds(interval.seconds)` (`domain/session/SessionControllerImpl.kt`) as a defense-in-depth check against `SamplingInterval.ALLOWED_SECONDS`; an out-of-set value returns `SessionStartOutcome.PermissionDenied` — this branch is structurally unreachable through the public API today.

### Session start — permission-gated, persist-before-collect

- `SessionControllerImpl.startSession(interval)` (`domain/session/SessionControllerImpl.kt`):
  1. Rejects (`PermissionDenied`) if `interval.seconds` is not in `SamplingInterval.ALLOWED_SECONDS`.
  2. Rejects (`PermissionDenied`) if `isBackgroundLocationGranted()` returns `false` — checked strictly before any DB write.
  3. Generates a UUID session id, inserts a `TrackingSessionEntity(status = ACTIVE)` via `TrackingSessionDao.insert`.
  4. Only then calls `LocationServiceController.start(sessionId, interval)` — collection can never start before the session row exists.
- Returns `SessionStartOutcome.Started(sessionId)` on success.

### Session stop — stop-then-finalize

- `SessionControllerImpl.stopSession(sessionId)`:
  1. Stops the collection service first (`locationServiceController.stop`), so the point set read afterward is final.
  2. Reads all persisted points for the session.
  3. Runs `SegmentClassifier.classify(points)` and `StatsEngine.averageSpeedMetersPerSecond`/`totalDistanceMeters`.
  4. Persists the session as `FINISHED` with `endTimestamp` (last point's timestamp, or `clock()` if no points), `stoppedTimeMillis`, `movingTimeMillis`, `averageSpeedMetersPerSecond`, `distanceMeters`.
- If no session row exists for `sessionId`, `stopSession` returns without effect (guards a stale/unknown id).

### Point collection — per-point guards + drift tracking

- `LocationCollector.start()` (`service/LocationCollector.kt`) refuses to request fixes at all unless `isLocationPermissionGranted()` AND `isSessionActive()` both hold, checked once before `LocationSampleSource.start` is ever invoked.
- Every individual fix is re-checked against `collecting` and `isSessionActive()` before being persisted — a session stopped mid-flight cannot leak a late point in.
- `observedIntervalDriftMillis` = `(sample.timestamp - previousAcceptedTimestamp) - configuredIntervalMillis`; `null` for a session's first accepted point (no predecessor).
- The first accepted point (and only the first) triggers `onFirstPointRecorded`, which feeds `FirstPointGeocodingCoordinator`.

### Stop vs. moving classification — inclusive radius, exclusive duration

`SegmentClassifier.classify` (`domain/stats/SegmentClassifier.kt`) partitions a session's point
stream into contiguous inter-point **intervals**, each `STOPPED` or `MOVING`, such that
`stoppedTimeMillis + movingTimeMillis` always equals total elapsed time by construction (the
intervals exactly tile `[first.timestamp, last.timestamp)` with no gaps/overlaps).

| Axis | Threshold | Boundary | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| Radius from window anchor | `STOP_RADIUS_METERS = 150.0` (Haversine, `DistanceCalculator`) | `distance <= 150.0` | still "contained" → window can extend |
| Window duration | `STOP_DURATION_MILLIS = 300_000` (5 min) | `duration > 300_000` (strict) | qualifies as `STOPPED`; a window of exactly 300_000ms is `MOVING` |
| Points < 2 | — | — | empty result; elapsed/stopped/moving times all `0` |

- Algorithm: greedy anchor-and-probe — for each anchor point, extend the window while every subsequent point stays within 150m of the anchor; if the resulting window's duration exceeds 300s, mark every interval in it `STOPPED` and continue from the window's end; otherwise advance the anchor by one point.
- `stopRadiusMeters`/`stopDurationMillis` are overridable parameters (defaulting to the constants above) — `UserSettings.stopRadiusMeters`/`stopDurationMillis` (`data/settings/SettingsRepository.kt`) can carry user-tuned values through the same signature, though production call sites (`SessionControllerImpl.stopSession`, `CsvExporter.export`) currently call `classify(points)` with no override, i.e. always the fixed 150m/300s constants.
- `stopLocations`: one `StopLocation` per contiguous run of `STOPPED` intervals (not one per interval), using the run's first anchor coordinate — for map-pin rendering.
- To extend: pass different `stopRadiusMeters`/`stopDurationMillis` to `classify()`, or read them from `UserSettings` at the call site.

### Stats — pure, recomputed, never persisted per point

`StatsEngine` (`domain/stats/StatsEngine.kt`), all pure functions over an ascending-by-timestamp point list:

| Function | Formula | Edge case |
|---|---|---|
| `instantSpeedMetersPerSecond(previous, current)` | Haversine distance / Δt seconds | `0.0` if `Δt <= 0` |
| `instantSpeeds(points)` | one value per consecutive pair | empty list if `< 2` points |
| `totalDistanceMeters(points)` | sum of consecutive-pair Haversine distances | `0.0` if `< 2` points |
| `elapsedTimeMillis(points)` | `last.timestamp - first.timestamp` | `0` if `<= 1` point |
| `averageSpeedMetersPerSecond(points)` | `totalDistanceMeters / elapsedSeconds` | `0.0` if `< 2` points or `elapsedSeconds <= 0` |

- Per-point derived values (instant speed, segment status) are never written to `GpsPointEntity` — always recomputed from raw lat/lon/timestamp, so a re-run of `SegmentClassifier` against an amended point set never disagrees with a stale stored value.
- Same functions drive both live UI (`TrackingViewModel`, recomputed on every Room `Flow` emission) and after-the-fact display (`SessionDetailViewModel`), guaranteeing identical numbers in both places.

### Export — finished-only, two fixed formats

`ExportService.export(sessionId, format)` (`domain/export/ExportService.kt`):
- Throws `NoSuchElementException` if the session doesn't exist.
- Throws `IllegalStateException` if `session.status != FINISHED` — export is never available for an active session.
- `ExportFormat.GPX` → `GpxExporter.export(points)`: GPX 1.1, one `<trkpt lat lon>` per point with an ISO-8601 `<time>`; throws `IllegalArgumentException` on an empty point list.
- `ExportFormat.CSV` → `CsvExporter.export(sessionId, points)`: header `session_id,timestamp,latitude,longitude,accuracy,speed_instant,segment_status`; `speed_instant` for point `i>=1` is the instant speed vs. point `i-1` (point `0` is `0.0`); `segment_status` for point `i>=1` inherits the classification of interval `[i-1, i]` (point `0` borrows interval `[0,1]`'s status; a single-point session defaults to `moving`); status literals are the fixed English strings `moving`/`stopped`.
- Output file name: `session-<sessionId>.gpx` or `.csv`, written under `context.filesDir/exports` (`AppNavigation.kt`'s `SessionDetailRoute.onExport`).

### Reverse geocoding — best-effort, at most once

`FirstPointGeocodingCoordinator.onFirstPointRecorded` (`domain/geocoding/FirstPointGeocodingCoordinator.kt`):
- Launches the geocode attempt on a supplied `CoroutineScope`, fire-and-forget — returns before the attempt resolves, so it never blocks point collection or session start/stop.
- Any exception from `ReverseGeocoder.reverseGeocode` is caught via `runCatching` and discarded.
- A `null` or blank result is treated identically to a failure — `TrackingSessionDao.updateLocationName` is never called, and the session's `locationName` stays `null`.
- Called at most once per session (guaranteed by `LocationCollector` invoking `onFirstPointRecorded` only for the first accepted point) — there is no retry path anywhere in the codebase.

### GPS precision — read once at session start

- `GpsPrecision` (`domain/model/GpsPrecision.kt`) is `HIGH_ACCURACY` or `BALANCED`, mapped by `GpsPrecision.toLocationRequestPriority()` (`service/LocationForegroundService.kt`) to Play Services' `Priority` constants.
- `LocationForegroundService.onStartCommand` reads `settingsRepository.userSettings.first().gpsPrecision` exactly once per session start, before building the `LocationRequest` — a settings change mid-session never mutates the already-running request.

### Location permission — check only, request lives in UI

- `LocationPermissionManager` (`permission/LocationPermissionManager.kt`) only checks grant state, never requests: `isFineLocationGranted()`, `isBackgroundLocationGranted()` (requires fine location AND, on API 29+/`Build.VERSION_CODES.Q`, `ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION`; below Q, fine location alone suffices).
- The actual runtime permission request dialog is triggered from `ui/navigation/AppNavigation.kt`'s `NewSessionRoute`, reactively — only after `NewSessionViewModel` surfaces a permission-denied state, not proactively on screen load.
- On API 30+ (`Build.VERSION_CODES.R`), only `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` is requested in that dialog (the two-step background-location flow is not implemented); if background location is still missing, the permission-denied message is shown again rather than crashing.

### User settings — typed defaults, DataStore-backed

`UserSettings` (`data/settings/SettingsRepository.kt`) defaults when nothing has ever been persisted:

| Field | Default |
|---|---|
| `samplingInterval` | `SamplingInterval.ONE_SECOND` |
| `speedUnit` | `SpeedUnit.KMH` |
| `distanceUnit` | `DistanceUnit.KM` |
| `stopRadiusMeters` | `SegmentClassifier.STOP_RADIUS_METERS` (150.0) |
| `stopDurationMillis` | `SegmentClassifier.STOP_DURATION_MILLIS` (300_000) |
| `gpsPrecision` | `GpsPrecision.HIGH_ACCURACY` |
| `keepScreenOnEnabled` | `true` |
| `defaultExportFormat` | `ExportFormat.GPX` |

- An unparsable/unknown persisted enum name (e.g. from a future removed enum member) falls back to the same default rather than crashing (`runCatching { Enum.valueOf(name) }.getOrNull() ?: defaults.field`).
- The underlying `DataStore<Preferences>` is memoized per file name (`SettingsRepository.Companion.dataStoreFor`), so multiple `SettingsRepository` instances for the same file never race.
